sections.title: Hobbies
sections.content: To say what you enjoy, put 'me gusta' in front of the plain infinitive: 'me gusta correr'. 'Me encanta' is the stronger version — I love it. Both stay in that one form when a verb follows, however many things you list: 'me gusta leer y escuchar música'.

sections.title: Where, when, and what it is like

items.spanish: A mí me gusta mucho correr.
Me encanta sacar fotos y montar en bicicleta.
items.english: I love taking photos and riding my bike.

items.spanish: Normalmente voy al parque los sábados.
items.english: I usually go to the park on Saturdays.

items.spanish: Todos están contentos porque no trabajan hoy.
items.english: Everyone is happy because they're not working today.

sections.content: 'Me gusta' is not 'I like' word for word — it is closer to 'it pleases me'. That is why it never changes shape in front of a verb, and why the person doing the liking is 'me', 'te' or 'le' rather than yo, tú or él.
